## Passing Data to RTMB (Option 1)

- Only the parameters argument as a list can be passed to `MakeADFun`
- One option is to write a wrapper function
- By using a wrapper function, we force the data into the objective function's parent environment

```{r}

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
sox <- read.csv("../data/sockeye/SRDATA2026 1.csv")
stock <- read.csv("../data/sockeye/FC_StockInfo 2.csv")
sox <- sox %>% left_join(stock, by = "PopID")
sox <- sox %>% filter(!is.na(spawners), !is.na(recruits))
sox <- sox %>% group_by(PopName) %>% mutate(sd_spawners = sd(spawners),  spawners_scaled = spawners/sd_spawners) %>% ungroup() %>% mutate(logRS = log(recruits/spawners))
```


```{r}
#| echo: true

library(RTMB)

param <- list(logsigma = 0, alpha = 0, logbeta = 0)

objective_function <- \(pars, data){
  getAll(pars, data)
  mu <- alpha - exp(logbeta)*spawners
  sigma <- exp(logsigma)

  nll <- -sum(dnorm(logRS, mu, sigma, log = TRUE))
  return(nll)
}

join_fun <- function(f, data) function(pars) f(pars, data)
stellako <- sox %>% filter(PopName == "Stellako")
obj_stellako <- MakeADFun(join_fun(objective_function, stellako), param, silent = TRUE)
fit_stellako <- nlminb(obj_stellako$par, obj_stellako$fn, obj_stellako$gr)

latestuart <- sox %>% filter(PopName == "Late Stuart")
obj_latestuart <- MakeADFun(join_fun(objective_function, latestuart), param, silent = TRUE)
fit_latestuart <- nlminb(obj_latestuart$par, obj_latestuart$fn, obj_latestuart$gr)
```

## Passing Data to RTMB (Option 2)

- Pass the data to the function environment
- Helpful for package development

```{r}
#| echo: true 

objective_function <- \(pars){
  getAll(pars, data)
  mu <- alpha - exp(logbeta)*spawners
  sigma <- exp(logsigma)

  nll <- -sum(dnorm(logRS, mu, sigma, log = TRUE))
  return(nll)
}

make_adfun <- function(pars, data){
  data_env <- new.env()
  
  ## The entire function's environment
  # environment(objective_function) <- environment()  
  
  ## Just data:
  data_env <- local({data <- data; environment()})
  environment(objective_function) <- data_env
  
  obj <- MakeADFun(objective_function, param, silent = TRUE)
  obj
}

nadina <- sox %>% filter(PopName == "Nadina")
obj_nadina <- make_adfun(param, nadina)
fit_nadina <- nlminb(obj_nadina$par, obj_nadina$fn, obj_nadina$gr)
```

## Fixing Overload Errors

- You might find a bug of "Invalid argument to 'advector' (lost class attribute?)"
- A quick solution to this is to make sure any functions written in R have an AD overload operator added
- Required for all functions within a package!

```{r}
#| echo: true

myfunc <- \(par){
"c" <- ADoverload("c")
"diag<-" <- ADoverload("diag<-")
# The rest of the function...
}
```

## Things with no gradient

- You can't use uniform distributions in RTMB as they have discontinuities at their end points.
- No while loops if the number of iterations depends on parameters
- No if statements that depend on parameter values
- Dimension and number of operations must be set
- If they change there are ***tricks*** that involve retaping each iteration or overloading

```{r}
fn <- function(x){
  if(x < 0) -1/2
  else 1/5
}
# fnt <- MakeTape(fn, 0.5)

fn <- function(theta){
  -dunif(theta, 0, 1,log = TRUE)
}
# fnt <- MakeTape(fn, 0.5)
```

## Forcing AD Overload

```{r}
#| echo: true

f <- function(x) {
  "if" <- ADoverload("if")
  if (x > 0) {
    3*x^2
  } else {
    x + x^2
  }
}

F <- MakeTape(f, 1)
F(2)
F(-2)
F$jacobian(2)
F$jacobian(-100)

## This isn't going to work
f <- function(x) {
  "if" <- ADoverload("if")
  if(x > 5){ 
    sum(dpois((x-5):(x+5), 5))
  }else{
    sum(dpois(0:x, 3))
  }
}
```
